value.rationale: The exact coupling metric at minimal regular degree 2 gives a quantitative boundary to general high-degree UST/1-out approximation. The natural family of orientation biases has two different, nontrivial sharp optimal sparse scales (ln2 versus 1), expressing metric sensitivity of the same Poisson missing-edge transition. The result is an infinite-parameter structural classification, not a single finite comparison; it does not pretend to cover arbitrary graphs.
